result.question: Our failure mode list for transformers looks thin to me. Pull the failure modes we currently have on file for a transformer, then suggest up to 4 more that an oil-immersed unit like Transformer 1 at site MAIN could realistically develop, such as corrosive sulfur deposition or bushing faults. For each suggested mode, tell me which of these channels would detect it: hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene, acetylene, co, co2, oxygen, nitrogen, dbds, dielectric_rigidity, interfacial_v, oti, oti_a, oti_t, ati, il1, il2, il3 or inut. Also check whether those channels actually have data between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000. Recommend adding only the modes that at least one channel with data can detect, and tell me which ones you left out and why. Don't recommend anything that duplicates an existing mode, even if the wording is different, and don't change the stored list yourself. If none of the suggestions survive, say that the current list stands.
result.answer:
The stored list stays as it is. I didn't write anything to it.

**Failure modes on file for transformer (9, marked as not complete):**
1. Partial Discharge in Oil
2. Thermal Fault — Oil Overheating
3. Thermal Fault — Core/Winding
4. Low-Energy Arcing (Sparking)
5. High-Energy Arcing
6. Tap Changer Mechanical Wear
7. Oil Contamination / Moisture Ingress
8. Cellulose Insulation Ageing
9. Oil Dielectric Degradation

**Data check for Transformer 1 at MAIN, 2024-01-15 to 2024-01-19:** The end time is exclusive, so there are 4 daily records (Jan 15–18). All 20 channels you listed have values in every one of them.

**Suggested modes and which channels detect them:**

| # | Suggested mode | Channels that detect it | Any with data? | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Corrosive sulfur / copper sulphide deposition (DBDS-driven) | dbds (main indicator); dielectric_rigidity (conductive deposits lower it); later hydrogen and ethylene once turn-to-turn heating or discharge starts | Yes | **Add** |
| 2 | Cooling system failure (fans or pumps stopped, radiators blocked or valves shut) | oti, oti_a, oti_t, read against ati (oil temperature rising while ambient and load stay flat) | Yes | **Add** |
| 3 | Phase load imbalance / excessive neutral current (unbalanced or harmonic-rich load, sustained overload) | il1, il2, il3, inut; then oti and oti_a as it heats the unit | Yes | **Add** |
| 4 | Bushing insulation fault (condenser core breakdown, bushing oil leak or moisture) | None of the listed channels | No | **Left out** |

**Why none of the three I'm recommending duplicate what's on file:**
- **Corrosive sulfur** is a specific chemical way the insulation fails. "Oil Dielectric Degradation", "Oil Contamination / Moisture Ingress" and "Cellulose Insulation Ageing" don't cover it.
- **Cooling system failure** is an outside equipment fault that heats all the oil. "Thermal Fault — Oil Overheating" is an internal hot spot identified from the gas pattern in the oil. It's the closest overlap of the three, so if you read that existing mode broadly, you could drop this one.
- **Load imbalance / neutral current** is a problem with how the unit is loaded, seen in the currents. None of the existing modes are based on current readings.

**What I left out and why:**
- **Bushing faults:** Bushings have their own sealed oil, so a fault there doesn't show up in the main-tank gas readings (hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene, acetylene, co, co2, oxygen, nitrogen). The oil-quality and temperature readings don't pick it up either. You'd need bushing capacitance or power-factor monitoring, and that isn't one of the listed channels.
- **Ideas I dropped as duplicates:**
  - Oil oxidation or sludge (interfacial_v, oxygen, co2) is already covered by "Oil Dielectric Degradation".
  - Air ingress through a failed gasket or seal (oxygen, nitrogen) is essentially "Oil Contamination / Moisture Ingress".
  - Core circulating currents or multiple core grounding is already "Thermal Fault — Core/Winding".

**Recommended additions:** Corrosive Sulfur / Copper Sulphide Deposition; Cooling System Failure; Phase Load Imbalance / Excessive Neutral Current.
